topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy along with their systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit specific cancer cell weaknesses, including hormone dependence, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic driver kinases and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogene-addicted kinases with small molecule inhibitors and the diverse molecular mechanisms underlying treatment resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the design and therapeutic mechanisms of targeted naked monoclonal antibodies and cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-based immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for immune surveillance and explain therapeutic strategies designed to re-engage or engineer T cells against tumor cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review broad clinical challenges, historical mortality trends, emerging paradigms like prevention and early detection, and ethical dilemmas in clinical trial design.
